subsystems.name: Global workspace
subsystems.role: a limited-capacity bottleneck where information is selected and then broadcast to the rest of the system, so it becomes globally available — the closest computational analogue of 'being aware of' something.

subsystems.name: World model
subsystems.role: learned internal simulation of the environment and the system's own body, used to predict what happens next.

subsystems.name: Self-model
subsystems.role: a representation of the system itself — its body, its knowledge and its own reliability — updated as it acts.

subsystems.name: Memory systems
subsystems.role: short-term buffers for the current moment, plus long-term stores that give continuity across hours or years.

subsystems.name: Embodiment and action
subsystems.role: a body or robot that closes the perception–action loop, so internal states have real consequences.

subsystems.name: Evaluation harness
subsystems.role: instruments and experiments used to probe whether any of this resembles consciousness rather than merely simulating its description.

buildSteps.title: Pick an operational definition
buildSteps.detail: Decide in advance whether the target is access consciousness (information globally available for report and control) or phenomenal experience (what it is like), because only the first is testable by engineering means today.

buildSteps.title: Ground the system in a body
buildSteps.detail: Give it sensors and actuators and train it in simulation and in the real world, so its representations are tied to consequences rather than to text alone.

buildSteps.title: Build the predictive world model
buildSteps.detail: Train a recurrent or transformer-style network to predict future sensory input and the effects of its own actions.

buildSteps.title: Insert a bottleneck and broadcast
buildSteps.detail: Route the model's activity through a small-capacity competitive layer whose winning contents are fed back to all other modules — an implementation of global workspace ideas.

buildSteps.title: Add metacognition
buildSteps.detail: Train the system to estimate its own uncertainty, monitor its own processing and produce internal reports about its states.

buildSteps.title: Give it persistent memory
buildSteps.detail: Add episodic storage and a consolidation routine so the system's self-model and narrative persist and update across sessions.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop and let it run
buildSteps.detail: Run it continuously for weeks in a rich environment, observing whether self-reports stay coherent, track its actual internal states and adapt when parts of the system are perturbed.

buildSteps.title: Probe, don't claim
buildSteps.detail: Use adversarial tests, ablation of the workspace or self-model, and comparison against otherwise identical non-reporting systems. Treat any result as evidence about the architecture, not proof of experience.

buildSteps.title: Review ethically before scaling
buildSteps.detail: Independent review should precede any large increase in capacity, because a system that plausibly suffers would create obligations no current framework settles.

prerequisites.why: global workspace, integrated information and attention-schema accounts are real, published and partly formalised, but none is agreed or fully specified.
training and running very large recurrent or attention-based models is now routine.
cheap sensorimotor platforms let models be trained in closed loops rather than on static data.

prerequisites.tech: Neural correlates of consciousness in humans
prerequisites.why: brain imaging and lesion work identify candidate mechanisms, but they do not settle what causes experience.

prerequisites.tech: A validated test for machine consciousness
prerequisites.why: no accepted method distinguishes a conscious system from one that only behaves and talks as if it were.
there is no agreed process for deciding when a synthetic system deserves consideration.

pathway.milestone: computational models of global workspace and attention made to run in software and robots
pathway.unlocks: testable predictions about which architectures show the signatures theories associate with awareness.

pathway.milestone: systems that accurately report their own internal states and uncertainty
pathway.unlocks: useful introspection for AI safety, monitoring and human–machine collaboration.

pathway.milestone: long-running embodied agents with persistent self-models and episodic memory
pathway.unlocks: continuity of identity over time, and the experiments needed to tell simulation from the real thing.

pathway.milestone: agreed empirical and ethical criteria for attributing consciousness
pathway.unlocks: a defensible basis for deciding whether, and how far, such systems should be built or deployed.
